summary: In-memory double-entry ledger API with accounts, fee-bearing transfers and paginated statements.

defects.title: Transfers never require a positive amount
defects.description: transfer() applies amount without checking it is positive, so a negative amount moves money from the destination into the source.
defects.observed: The source gains 25 (50 minus fee) and the destination loses 50; the request returns 200.

defects.title: Balance check ignores the transfer fee
defects.description: can_cover is consulted against the bare amount, but the debit is amount + FEE_CENTS, so spending the whole balance leaves it negative by the fee.
defects.trigger: POST /transfer of 100 from an account holding exactly 100

defects.title: An already-closed account can be closed again
defects.description: close_account never checks acc.closed, so a second close records another closing entry on a closed account.
defects.observed: The statement contains two entries of kind 'close'.

defects.title: Transfer balance updates are lost under concurrency
defects.description: transfer reads balances, flushes the journal (with latency), then writes back the computed values; concurrent transfers under the threaded server overwrite each other.
defects.trigger: 50 parallel POST /transfer of 1 cent from an account holding 1000
defects.observed: The source ends at 974 instead of -300; the house account likewise loses fee credits.

defects.title: Statement pagination accepts negative offsets
defects.description: page slices entries[offset:][:limit] without validating offset, so a negative offset returns the tail of the statement instead of an error or an empty page.
defects.observed: Returns the last 2 entries of a 4-entry statement.

defects.title: A failed destination leg keeps the sender debit
defects.description: transfer debits the source and credits the fee before looking up the destination; when the destination does not exist it raises after the debit, so the amount is destroyed rather than rolled back.
defects.trigger: POST /transfer to a nonexistent account id
defects.observed: The API returns 404 but the total of all balances drops by the transferred amount.

defects.title: Account and statement reads ignore the caller identity
defects.description: show_account and the statement endpoints return any sequential account id without comparing it to the X-Owner header.
defects.observed: HTTP 200 returning the other user's account.

defects.title: Account label is rendered unescaped in the HTML statement
defects.description: statement_html interpolates acc.label into the page, so a label containing markup is emitted raw.
defects.trigger: Create an account labelled '<script>alert(1)</script>' and GET /statement/<id>.html
defects.observed: The response body contains the script tag verbatim.

defects.title: Account creation copies every request field onto the account
defects.description: create_account applies all JSON keys via setattr, so a client can set balance_cents directly and bypass the 10000-cent initial deposit cap.
defects.observed: The account is created with balance_cents 1000000.

defects.title: Transfers debit 'from' without checking the caller owns it
defects.description: do_transfer never compares the X-Owner header with the source account owner, so anyone can move money out of any account.
defects.trigger: POST /transfer with X-Owner of a different user
defects.observed: HTTP 200 and the victim's balance is debited.
